subject: Greenspring discovery — model fit clarifications and streaming behavior
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: Discovery w/ Greenspring — streaming UX concerns and next steps

Thanks for joining the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed follow-ups so we don't lose momentum with Greenspring: 

Call highlights:
- Use case: real-time clinical triage assistant embedded in their clinician-facing portal. Must stream partial output as the model generates suggestions.
- Key constraints: strict latency SLO for first token (~150ms), deterministic stop behavior for signed-off recommendations, and occasional hallucination sensitivity (must avoid making unsafe recommendations).
- Procurement timeline: procurement team expects an internal eval + security questionnaire cleared in ~4 weeks.

Open technical items for us:
1) Model fit: they asked about model candidates that tradeoff latency vs. factuality (they called out partial output coherence as a blocker).
2) Stop sequences / partial tokens: they need a guarantee that streaming won't produce incomplete or truncated clinical advice when a stop token is encountered.
3) Benchmarks: they asked for concrete latency and partial-output coherence examples, plus a sample prompt set to run in their environment.

Proposed actions (owner):
- Karthik: put together a short candidate list (3 variants) with expected tail latency and incoherence failure modes. Include quantized variants if helpful. (ETA 2 business days)
- Marissa: prepare a one-page non-technical pilot plan and procurement-friendly checklist (ETA 3 business days).
- Hannah: share prompt set, attach pilot plan draft, and schedule follow-up with Alex. (I'll do a 30-min sync for Thursday morning)

Attachments: draft pilot plan stub attached (greenspring-pilot-plan.pdf) and initial prompt set (prompt-set-v1.jsonl).

Hannah
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, procurement@greenspringhealth.com
Date: 2027-04-12T08:10:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up + pilot artifacts for Greenspring evaluation

Alex — thanks again for the time yesterday. As promised, attaching a concise pilot plan and an initial prompt set you can use to run local checks. Two quick notes up-front:

1) Model recommendations (shortlist):
- rdx-small-qa (fast, lower cost) — good for deterministic templates, weaker on long-context factuality.
- rdx-medium-factual (balanced) — our recommended starting point for clinical triage pilots.
- rdx-large-guarded (best factuality/guardrails) — higher latency and cost but fewer hallucination edge-cases.

2) Streaming behavior and partial output: we observed in internal tests that partial outputs can become incoherent if prompts contain nested bullets and abrupt stop tokens. We'll provide a short benchmark demonstrating typical failure modes and suggested prompt engineering fixes (stop token placement + explicit finalizing instructions).

Attached:
- greenspring-pilot-plan.pdf (pilot steps, success metrics, timeline)
- prompt-set-v1.jsonl (sample prompts and expected outputs)

Live links:
- Evaluation folder: https://drive.redwood.example.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-greenspring-eval
- Shared eval in Redwood: https://app.redwood.example.com/evals/GS-2027-042

Can we book 30 minutes tomorrow 10–10:30am PT for a short walkthrough and to confirm the success criteria? I'll include Karthik for the model recommendation discussion.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@greenspringhealth.com>

Cc: procurement@greenspringhealth.com
Date: 2027-04-12T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up + pilot artifacts for Greenspring evaluation

Hannah — thanks for the follow-up and the artifacts. A few clarifying questions from our side before the walkthrough: 

1) Partial-output risk: our clinicians flagged a scenario where streaming produced an instruction fragment (e.g., "...consider starting the patient on") that was then completed incorrectly by a later token. Can you point to a clear mitigation—either model-level or UX-level—to prevent presenting an incomplete recommendation?

2) Stop sequences: what are the guarantees if the session gets cut mid-generation? We need guidance on making recommendations atomic in the UI (so clinicians never see dangling partial sentences).

3) Benchmarks: the Drive folder is empty for me — I see the link but no files. Can you re-share the specific latency/partial-coherence report and the annotated prompt examples? We want something we can paste into our internal evaluation harness.

Procurement note: they asked whether you support SOC 2 and if we can get a redacted AOC during the pilot. Procurement looped me in on this thread (procurement@greenspringhealth.com).

Alex Rivera

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@greenspringhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, procurement@greenspringhealth.com
Date: 2027-04-12T09:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up + pilot artifacts for Greenspring evaluation

Alex — great questions, answers below plus a short next-step checklist.

1) Partial-output risk — mitigations:
- Model-level: recommend rdx-medium-factual or rdx-large-guarded for production. They have lower perplexity on clinical completion tasks; we can pin a response-length budget and enable prefix/KV caching so the runtime stops streaming until a finalizing token is generated in most cases.
- UX-level: render streaming as "draft" lines in the UI (gray, non-actionable) until a finalizing token or explicit completion signal arrives. Only promote content to actionable UI when the streaming engine emits the finalization marker. This avoids exposing clinicians to mid-sentence guidance.

2) Stop sequences / session cuts:
- Operationally, we recommend embedding an explicit end-of-recommendation token in prompts (e.g., "<END_RECOMMENDATION>") and post-process client-side to suppress output until that token is observed. For higher safety, use the runtime's canary fallback: if a session is interrupted before finalization, return the previous validated state and surface an "incomplete result" banner in the UI.

3) Benchmarks and files: sorry about the Drive visibility — I had not finalized permissions. I've moved the latency/partial-coherence report and an annotated prompt set into the folder and set view access to your domain. You should now see:
- gs-latency-coherence-report-20270412.pdf
- greenspring-annotated-prompts-v1.jsonl

Procurement / compliance:
- Yes — we are SOC 2 Type II and can share a redacted AOC during the pilot. I'll loop in our security contact once you confirm the NDAs.

Next steps (proposed):
- Confirm pilot start (we can begin a 2-week evaluation sandbox) — can you confirm by EOD Tuesday?
- 30-min walkthrough tomorrow 10–10:30am PT (I will send calendar invite).
- Karthik to send the detailed model tradeoff table after the walkthrough.

Attachments (now shared in Drive): gs-latency-coherence-report-20270412.pdf, greenspring-annotated-prompts-v1.jsonl
